title: Lotus Booking — a booking app for a local yoga studio
summary: A simple website where students can see the weekly class timetable, book a spot in a class, and cancel if plans change. The studio owner gets a small dashboard to add classes and see who is coming.
audience: Students of a small neighbourhood yoga studio, and the studio owner who manages classes.
features: Weekly class timetable anyone can browse
Book or cancel a spot in a class
Class capacity so classes can't be overbooked
Owner dashboard to add, edit and cancel classes
userFlow: A student opens the website and sees this week's classes
They pick a class and tap "Book my spot"
If they're new, they create an account with their email
They get a confirmation and see the class in "My bookings"
The owner sees the booking in their dashboard

stack.name: React + Vite
stack.why: The most popular way to build web pages today, so your coding agent knows it inside out and help is easy to find.

stack.name: Tailwind CSS
stack.why: Lets your agent style pages quickly without writing separate design files.

stack.name: Supabase
stack.why: Gives you sign-in and a database for bookings with a generous free tier — no server to manage.

stack.name: Cloudflare Pages
stack.why: Free, fast hosting that updates automatically every time you save to GitHub.

setup.modelAdvice: With 16GB of RAM on your Mac, a model like Qwen2.5-Coder 7B runs comfortably on your own computer through Ollama. It's free and private. If it ever feels slow, you can switch your coding agent to a free cloud model instead — your code stays yours either way.

steps.title: Install a code editor
steps.explain: VS Code is a free app for viewing and editing your project files. Download it from code.visualstudio.com, or install it with Homebrew.
steps.expected:
==> Installing Cask visual-studio-code
🍺  visual-studio-code was successfully installed!

steps.title: Install Git
steps.explain: Git quietly keeps a history of every change you make, so you can always go back.

steps.title: Install Node.js
steps.explain: Node lets your computer run the tools that build modern websites.

steps.title: Install Ollama
steps.explain: Ollama runs AI models on your own computer, for free.

steps.title: Download your AI model
steps.explain: This downloads a coding model sized for your 16GB machine. It's a few gigabytes, so grab a cup of tea.

steps.title: Install your coding agent
steps.explain: OpenCode is a helper that lives in your terminal. You describe what you want, it writes the code.

build.intro: Paste each prompt into your coding agent, one at a time. Wait for it to finish and check the result before moving on — small steps make problems easy to fix.

prompts.title: Create the project
prompts.why: Starting from a clean, standard template means fewer surprises later.
prompts.prompt: Create a new React + Vite + TypeScript project called lotus-booking with Tailwind CSS set up. Add a simple home page that says "Lotus Yoga — Book your class". Then tell me the exact command to start it.
prompts.expected: A new lotus-booking folder, and the page opens at http://localhost:5173

prompts.title: Show the class timetable
prompts.why: Seeing classes is the heart of the app, so we build it first with sample data.
prompts.prompt: On the home page, show a weekly timetable of yoga classes grouped by day. Each class shows name, time, teacher and spots left. Use 8 sample classes stored in a local file for now. Make it look calm and friendly on mobile.
prompts.expected: A list of classes grouped by Monday–Sunday, readable on your phone

prompts.title: Connect accounts and data
prompts.why: Now we swap sample data for a real database so bookings are saved.
prompts.prompt: Connect this app to Supabase using environment variables VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY. Create tables for classes and bookings, with security rules so students only see their own bookings. Add email sign-in. Give me the SQL to paste into Supabase.
prompts.expected: A sign-in page works and classes load from your database

prompts.title: Book and cancel
prompts.why: This is the action students came for.
prompts.prompt: Add a "Book my spot" button on each class. Signed-in students can book once per class, and only if spots are left. Add a "My bookings" page where they can cancel.
prompts.expected: Booking a class lowers the spots left; it appears under My bookings

prompts.title: Owner dashboard
prompts.why: The owner needs a simple way to run the timetable.
prompts.prompt: Add an /admin page only the studio owner can open (check an is_owner flag in a profiles table). The owner can add, edit and cancel classes and see the list of who booked each class.
prompts.expected: Signed in as the owner, you can add a class and see it on the timetable

explainer: Git is like a save button with memory — every time you save, it remembers exactly what changed.
GitHub is a safe online folder that remembers every version of your project. If your laptop breaks, your work is still there.
Your hosting provider watches your GitHub folder and puts the newest version online automatically.

steps.title: Start tracking your project
steps.explain: Tells Git to start remembering changes in this folder.

steps.title: Make your first save
steps.explain: Takes a snapshot of everything with a short note about what it is.
steps.command: git add . && git commit -m "First version of Lotus Booking"
steps.expected: [main (root-commit) a1b2c3d] First version of Lotus Booking

steps.title: Create your GitHub folder
steps.explain: Sign up free at github.com, click "New repository", name it lotus-booking and leave it empty. Then connect it:

steps.title: Upload to GitHub
steps.explain: Sends your saved snapshot up to GitHub.
steps.command: git branch -M main && git push -u origin main

launch.recommendation: For a small studio, Cloudflare Pages + Supabase costs nothing until you have thousands of students. Buying your domain from Cloudflare keeps everything in one place with no markup.

steps.title: Connect GitHub to Cloudflare Pages
steps.explain: In Cloudflare, go to Workers & Pages → Create → Pages → Connect to Git, and choose lotus-booking. Use these build settings:
steps.command:
Build command: npm run build
Output folder: dist
steps.expected: Success! Your site is live at lotus-booking.pages.dev

steps.title: Add your secret settings
steps.explain: Your live site needs the same database details as your computer. Add them under Settings → Environment variables.
steps.expected: Classes load on your live site

steps.title: Add your own domain (optional)
steps.explain: Buy lotusyoga.ie (or similar) and add it under Custom domains. Cloudflare sets everything up for you.
steps.command: Custom domains → Set up a domain → lotusyoga.ie
steps.expected: Active — your app is live at your own address 🎉

nodes.name: Your website
nodes.label: THE FRONT DOOR
nodes.purpose: The screens students see and tap: the timetable, the book button, My bookings.
nodes.connects: Talks to the accounts & data service over a secure connection whenever someone signs in or books.
nodes.prerequisites: Node.js and a code editor installed (Set up phase).
nodes.alternatives: Vue or Svelte instead of React; Netlify or Vercel instead of Cloudflare Pages.

nodes.name: Accounts & data
nodes.label: THE FILING CABINET
nodes.purpose: Remembers who each student is, the classes, and every booking — safely, so students only see their own.
nodes.connects: Answers requests from your website: sign-ins, class lists, new bookings.
nodes.prerequisites: A free Supabase account; your website built enough to ask it questions.

nodes.name: Your AI helper
nodes.label: THE ASSISTANT
nodes.purpose: The model that writes the code when your coding agent asks it to.
nodes.connects: Runs on your own computer; your coding agent sends it your prompts.
nodes.alternatives: A free cloud model if your computer feels slow.

nodes.name: Your coding agent
nodes.label: THE BUILDER
nodes.purpose: You describe what you want in plain English; it turns that into real code in your project.
nodes.connects: Reads and writes your project files; asks your AI helper for the code.

nodes.name: Your safety copy
nodes.label: THE VAULT
nodes.purpose: Keeps every version of your project safe online, so nothing is ever lost.
nodes.connects: Your computer pushes saved versions up; your hosting watches it for new versions.
nodes.prerequisites: Git installed and a free GitHub account.

nodes.name: Your hosting
nodes.label: THE SHOPFRONT
nodes.purpose: Puts your website on the internet so anyone can visit it, day or night.
nodes.connects: Watches your safety copy on GitHub and publishes the newest version automatically.
nodes.prerequisites: Your project pushed to GitHub (Save to GitHub phase).

nodes.name: Your own address
nodes.label: THE SIGN ABOVE THE DOOR
nodes.purpose: A memorable address like lotusyoga.ie instead of the free .pages.dev one.
nodes.alternatives: Porkbun, or skip it and use the free address.
